description: Tiny automation pipelines. Bring CI/CD to the smallest projects. Self-hosted, Lightweight, CLI only.

summary.one_liner: Pipelight is a small Rust CLI that runs automation pipelines defined in TOML, HCL, YAML, or JavaScript/TypeScript, with optional triggers from git hooks and file changes.
summary.what_it_does: Pipelight lets you define pipelines as named steps that each run a list of shell commands. Pipelines can be written in TOML, HCL, YAML, or JavaScript/TypeScript, with TypeScript offering helper functions such as pipeline, step, and ssh. Triggers can be attached to pipelines, filtered by branch and git action such as pre-push or pre-commit. The README says the watcher and git hooks can be enabled through the CLI so pipelines run on file changes or git events. The pipelight logs command shows pipeline status, events, execution time, and step output, with a verbosity flag to show the raw output of every subprocess. The pipelight init command creates a default pipelight.ts config and pipelight run executes it.
use_cases: run build and test commands on git push or commit
run tests automatically when files change
deploy a built site to a host over ssh
automate repetitive project tasks from the terminal
replace a heavy CI setup for a small project
notable: Pipeline definitions in TOML, HCL, YAML, or JavaScript/TypeScript
Triggers on git hooks such as pre-push and pre-commit, filtered by branch
File-change watcher that can run pipelines automatically
Verbose logs with a flag that shows every subprocess output
Small binary of about 13 MB, CLI only
caveats: The README gives no details on platform support or installation beyond a link to a package manager guide that is not included
Documentation is referenced externally for a fuller guide
